title: The Dove, the Fox, and the Crane
logline: A fox bluffs a dove into throwing down her chicks until a heron teaches her that he cannot climb; the fox then flatters the heron into hiding his own head under his wing and eats him.
moral: It is easy to give good advice to others and still fail to guard yourself.
tone: Tender and funny for the first two thirds (a bully, a bluff, a brave little mother), then quiet suspense and a dry, dark ending played without gore.

beats.summary: A dove builds a nest at the top of a very tall palm beside a river.
Three chicks hatch; she feeds them and hardly leaves. CHICKS 3.
A fox shouts up: one chick, or I climb and eat you all.
She believes he can climb (her mistaken thought cloud).
She throws him a chick. CHICKS 2.
Days later he returns and she does the same. CHICKS 1.
Her grief; one tear falls all the way to the river.
The heron sees her and asks why she cries.
The heron: the fox cannot climb this palm.
The coaching: tell him to climb if he can; give nothing.
The dove stands firm and dares the fox.
The fox fails to climb, lands on his rump and is amazed.
The dove names and points out her adviser: the innocent mistake.
The fox flatters the heron and starts closing the distance.
Wind from every side: where does the head go?
Under my wing. Show me, begs the fox.
The heron hides his head: he cannot see.
The fox leaps and catches him.
You knew how to advise the dove but not how to protect yourself.
The fox eats him and goes; the river is quiet.

props.description: Library nest: build stages nb, eggs 3, chicks 3/2/1, rock.
A single free chick (the nest chick drawing as a standalone prop, about 34 wide) that can fall, flap stub wings and be held as a tuft in the fox mouth.

scenes.summary: Home is built: the dove brings twigs to the top of a very tall palm by the river, lays three eggs, waits through a day and a night, the chicks hatch and she feeds them. The heron is planted as a small figure fishing in the river.

camera.notes: Start FULL (700,615,z1.0) showing palm left and river right. 1.3 ease to WIDE_PALM (430,590,z1.15). 2.0-2.8 tilt up the trunk to NEST_MED (390,360,z1.9). 3.5-4.7 ease back to FULL so the river and the tiny heron read. 5.5 push to NEST_CLOSE (390,300,z2.6) and hold to 11.3. 11.8-14.2 NEST_MED so the feeding flights have room. 15.3-17.8 slow push back to NEST_CLOSE.

scenes.summary: One morning the fox arrives under the palm, looks all the way up and shouts his demand and his threat. The threat is a bluff, but he sells it by rearing against the trunk.

scenes.summary: The dove flutters down to the driftwood snag and tells her story. The heron shows her the truth in a thought cloud (the fox sliding down the trunk), then coaches her: stand tall, tell him to climb, give nothing.

scenes.summary: Next day. The fox comes for his usual delivery. The dove almost gives in from habit, then takes the brave pose and tells him to climb. He tries twice, slides down and lands on his rump. Shocked, he asks who taught her.

scenes.summary: The dove proudly names her adviser and points to him. The fox walks to the river, flatters the heron and asks his first wind question. The heron shows off the answer. With each exchange the fox is one step nearer.

scenes.summary: The second question: wind from every side. The heron explains that he puts his head under his wing. The fox begs to see it and creeps into leaping distance while the dove, far away on her palm, sees the danger and cannot be heard.

camera.notes: RIVER_TWO (about 930,720,z1.75), slow drift right 20 units over the scene. 124.4-127.0 pull to z1.5 for the swirling wind. 132.6 push to z1.9 on the pair. 135.2-136.3 one cutaway key to RIVER_WIDE with the palm top in the upper left for the dove warning, back by 137.2.

scenes.composition: Fox left, heron right, the gap between them visibly shorter than in S8 (two ticks, then one). Keep the fox face and the heron head both above y 760 world.

actions.action: Strokes his chin with a paw, thinking of the next question.
actions.acting: gaze up and away (acting thought), tail still

actions.action: Leans in; shuffles to the second tick (x 700 to 760), forepaws now in the shallows with small ripples.
actions.acting: the move is hidden inside the gesture

actions.action: Asks with both forepaws opening outward.
actions.acting: talk, brow -0.4 (false innocence)

actions.action: Wind from the left joins the wind from the right; then streaks from above.
actions.acting: reeds whip both ways out of phase

actions.action: Four arrows circle the heron and close in on him; the fox draws the circle in the air with a paw.
actions.acting: the heron crest and tail feathers blow about; he turns his head left, right, left: no side is safe

actions.action: The wind drops; the reeds swing back and settle (damped swing).
actions.acting: heron smooths his feathers

actions.action: Smiles with his eyes: an easy one. Raises a wing.
actions.acting: lid 0.4, crest up, chest out

actions.action: Taps his own head with the wing tip.
actions.acting: small precise tap, head bobs

actions.action: Lifts the wing to show the space under it and dips his head halfway toward it, then pops back up.
actions.acting: a half demonstration only: the tease before the real one

actions.action: Presses his forepaws together and begs, tail wagging.
actions.acting: big wet eyes (wet true as fake), brow -0.6

actions.action: While the heron looks up at the sky to enjoy the request, the fox tongue slides across his teeth; back to the smile when the heron looks down.
actions.acting: mask off, mask on

actions.action: Shuffles to the last tick (x 760 to 820); his haunches lower.
actions.acting: the body is already a crouch; the face still smiles

actions.action: Cutaway inside the shot: on the palm top the dove flaps and hops, beak wide open, small sound arcs that fade before they cross the river.
actions.acting: she saw his face at 105.5; now she tries to warn; nobody hears

actions.action: Does not look round. Clears his throat, shakes out the wing.
actions.acting: eyes shut with importance

actions.action: Nods: very well. Raises the wing high.
actions.acting: anticipation for the tuck; a last look at his audience, then eyes close

actions.action: Goes completely still; only his pupils follow the wing.
actions.acting: suspense by stillness

scenes.summary: The heron tucks his head under his wing and becomes a blind grey ball on two legs. The fox face changes, he crouches, leaps and has him. A comic dust cloud covers the impact; when it clears the heron is pinned under the fox paws.

camera.notes: RIVER_TWO z1.8, very slow push to z2.0 by 144.6 (the only motion in the frame besides the neck and the fox eyes). 145.64 keys on the take off and the landing (146.3) to follow the leap right; 146.3 panel-only shake 6 px for 4 frames. 148.7 ease to a close two-shot (1020,760,z2.3): fox head above, heron head below.

scenes.composition: Heron right of centre; fox left with the last tick under his paws. After the leap: fox on top at x 1040, heron pinned under his forepaws with the long neck and head lying toward the left of the frame so both faces read.

actions.action: Begins: the neck curls down in a slow S toward the raised wing.
actions.acting: eyes closed, serene

actions.action: The head goes in under the wing.
actions.acting: tuck to 0.8; crest plume the last thing to vanish

actions.action: The wing closes over it. He is a round feathered ball on two thin legs, swaying slightly.
actions.acting: tuck 1; breathe(); one leg lifts to the one-leg rest pose

actions.action: The smile slides off. Teeth. The pupils shrink and lock on.
actions.acting: mask off for good: brow 1, lid 0.3, ears flat

actions.action: Sinks into a full crouch, haunches wiggling, tail tip twitching.
actions.acting: anticipate held 1.9 s; sq 0.85

actions.action: From inside the ball, muffled and proud, one foot taps: see?
actions.acting: he thinks the lesson is going well

actions.action: Leaps: stretch on take off, a flat fast arc of 220 units.
actions.acting: sq 1.15, forepaws out, jaws open

actions.action: Impact inside a comic scuffle cloud: dust puffs, stars, one fox tail and one heron leg poking out, grey feathers flying; a column of splash drops.
actions.acting: softened: the catch itself is hidden
actions.library: fightCloud (planned effect), feather, drops, panel-only shake

actions.action: The cloud thins: the fox stands over the heron with both forepaws pinning the body.
actions.acting: chest heaving, grin, tail high

actions.action: His head pops out from under the wing: eyes huge, crest flat, beak open.
actions.acting: eyes wide, sq 0.9, looks up at the fox, then to camera for 5 frames

actions.action: Lowers his face close to the heron and speaks.
actions.acting: lid 0.5, smirk; slow and enjoying it

actions.action: Feathers drift down around them on a damped sway; ripples spread.
actions.acting: secondary motion

scenes.summary: The fox mocks him with the moral: you advised the dove but could not guard yourself. The eating happens behind the reeds. The fox leaves, passing under the palm without stopping; the river is quiet, one feather floats away, and the dove holds her last chick.

camera.notes: Close two-shot z2.3. 151.8-152.6 one eased key out to RIVER_WIDE so the palm and the tiny dove are in the top left when he names her; back in by 153.2. 156.44 the camera pans right and up into the reeds (1250,640,z1.8) away from the pair. 158.16 pull out to FULL (700,615,z1.0) and hold to the end. THE END sits in the sky between the palm crown and the right edge.

scenes.composition: Final picture: palm on the left with the dove and one chick on top, empty shallows on the right with fading rings where the heron stood, low orange sun over the water, one grey feather on the current.

actions.action: Speaks down to him, one paw lifted to count the points.
actions.acting: smirk, lid 0.5, unhurried

actions.action: Jerks his muzzle toward the far palm. An arrow runs across to the small dove on her nest.
actions.acting: the heron eyes follow the arrow

actions.action: Small on the palm: she stands frozen, wing over the chick, watching.
actions.acting: no movement at all

actions.action: Turns back and taps the heron on the beak with one claw.
actions.acting: two taps on the two stresses

actions.action: The eyes drop away from the fox; the crest sinks.
actions.acting: shame ending pattern: look up, then the gaze breaks and the head lowers

actions.action: Widest grin; ears up.
actions.acting: held 1 s

actions.action: Pan away into the reeds as the fox head goes down.
actions.acting: softened: the eating is never shown

actions.action: The reeds shake twice; GULP! in the reeds; three feathers rise above the reed tops.
actions.acting: one beat, no more

actions.action: Walks out of the reeds to the left with a round belly, a grey feather stuck on his nose; he blows it off.
actions.acting: satisfied, lid 0.6, slow walk

actions.action: Passes under the palm; glances up once. The dove takes the BRAVE pose. He keeps walking and leaves frame left by 160.4.
actions.acting: her lesson holds; he does not stop

actions.action: Wide and still: sky preset dusk, low sun, the rings where the heron stood fade out.
actions.acting: everything slows

actions.action: One grey feather lands on the water and drifts right on the current.
actions.acting: the only moving thing

actions.action: She looks at the empty shallows; her head lowers; she draws the chick in under her wing.
actions.acting: slow head drop, wet, long blink; no smile

actions.action: THE END title pops into the sky and holds to 164.7.
actions.acting: the feather keeps drifting under it

ending.description: After the last word (161.42) the wide dusk picture holds: palm with the dove and her one chick on the left, empty shallows with one drifting grey feather on the right. THE END pops into the sky at 162.0 and holds to 164.7.

subtitles.ar: بنت حمامة عشًّا عاليًا في نخلة قرب النهر.|وضعت فيه بيضًا، وانتظرت حتى خرج منه فراخ صغيرة.|كانت تطعمها كل يوم، ولا تترك العش إلا قليلًا.
subtitles.en: A dove built a nest high in a palm tree beside a river.|She laid eggs and waited until little chicks hatched.|She fed them each day and rarely left the nest.

subtitles.ar: وفي صباح، وقف ثعلب تحت النخلة وصاح:|«أعطيني فرخًا من فراخك، وإلا صعدت إلى الشجرة وأكلتكم جميعًا!»|خافت الحمامة، وظنت أن الثعلب يستطيع الوصول إليها،|فرمت إليه فرخًا.
subtitles.en: One morning, a fox stood beneath the palm tree and shouted,|“Give me one of your chicks, or I will climb up and eat all of you!”|The dove was frightened. She thought he could reach her,|so she dropped one chick to him.

subtitles.ar: عاد الثعلب بعد أيام، وهددها مرة أخرى.|ففعلت الحمامة الشيء نفسه، وحزنت حزنًا شديدًا.|رآها طائر مالك الحزين قرب النهر،|وسألها عن سبب بكائها.
subtitles.en: The fox came back a few days later and threatened her again.|The dove did the same thing and was deeply distressed.|A heron saw her near the river|and asked why she was crying.

subtitles.ar: حكت الحمامة ما جرى، فقال مالك الحزين:|«الثعلب لا يستطيع تسلق هذه النخلة!|عندما يعود، قولي له: اصعد إن استطعت.|لن أعطيك فراخي بيدي بعد اليوم.»
subtitles.en: The dove told him what had happened. The heron said,|“The fox cannot climb this palm tree!|When he returns, tell him to climb if he can.|You will not hand over your chicks again.”

subtitles.ar: جاء الثعلب في اليوم التالي، وكرر تهديده.|هذه المرة أجابته الحمامة بثبات:|«اصعد أنت إن كنت تستطيع! لن أرمي إليك شيئًا.»|تفاجأ الثعلب، وسألها: «من علمك هذا الكلام؟»
subtitles.en: The fox came the next day and repeated his threat.|This time the dove answered firmly,|“Climb up yourself if you can! I will not throw anything to you.”|The fox was surprised and asked, “Who taught you to say that?”

subtitles.ar: قالت الحمامة: «مالك الحزين الذي يعيش عند النهر.»|ذهب الثعلب إليه، وتظاهر بالإعجاب بذكائه.|سأله: «إذا جاءت الريح من اليمين، أين تضع رأسك؟»|فأجابه الطائر.
subtitles.en: “The heron who lives by the river,” the dove replied.|The fox went to him and pretended to admire his cleverness.|“If the wind blows from the right,” he asked, “where do you put your head?”|The bird answered.

subtitles.ar: ثم قال الثعلب:|«وماذا تفعل إذا جاءت الريح من كل الجهات؟»|قال مالك الحزين: «أضع رأسي تحت جناحي.»|طلب الثعلب أن يريه كيف يفعل ذلك، فوافق الطائر.
subtitles.en: Then the fox asked,|“And what do you do if the wind comes from every direction?”|The heron said, “I put my head under my wing.”|The fox asked him to demonstrate, and the bird agreed.

subtitles.ar: وما إن أخفى مالك الحزين رأسه تحت جناحه،|حتى قفز عليه الثعلب وأمسك به.|قال ساخرًا: «عرفت كيف تنصح الحمامة، لكنك لم تعرف كيف تحمي نفسك!»|ثم أكله ومضى، وبقي النهر هادئًا.
subtitles.en: As soon as the heron tucked his head beneath his wing,|the fox leaped on him and caught him.|“You knew how to advise the dove,” he mocked, “but not how to protect yourself!”|Then he ate him and went away, leaving the river quiet.

new_assets.name: heron
new_assets.description: Tall wading bird for this and any later heron, crane or stork fable. At s 1: feet at (x,y); two legs 150 long, 7 wide, yellow, with a backward knee at half height; body oval 150 x 90 centred 195 above the feet, grey-blue #8fa3c4 with blue Ben-Day shading and a darker wing oval 110 x 60; neck a white two-curve path 130 long; head 44 x 34 with a black cap stripe and a 50 long trailing plume; beak a yellow dagger 80 long. Pose fields: neck 0..1 (0.2 folded S for fishing, 1 fully stretched), headRot, talk, stab (fishing strike 0..1), wing 0..1 (near wing raised as a gesturing hand; a hand target wingTo [x,y] optional), tuck 0..1 (head travels along an arc to the wing root and the wing closes over it; at 1 no head or neck is visible), puff 0..1 (chest out), crest -1..1, ph/amp (wading steps), lift (one-leg rest), eyes open/wide/shut, brow, plus the shared acting fields.
new_assets.implementation: New file Library/cast/heron.js in the style of bird.js: shape() ovals for body and wing, seg() for legs with a knee point from simple 2 bone IK, the neck as a quadratic path stroked twice (ink 14, white 9) between the shoulder point and a head point computed from neck, headRot and tuck; eye2 for the eye so gaze, lid and wet work; draw order far leg, body, neck and head, near wing last so the wing covers the head when tuck = 1. Wrap with acting() and add a registry entry and catalogue poses (stand, fish, talk and wing up, tuck 0.5, tuck 1, wide eyed).

new_assets.name: dove (bird kind)
new_assets.description: A new kind 'dove' on the Library bird: white body, pale grey wing, black neck bar, pink beak and feet, no crest. Optional fields used here: puff 0..1 (chest out, the BRAVE pose), wing (near wing extended as a shelter or pointer; sag -0.8 already points), carry (planned 'bird carry' field: a twig or worm at the beak tip).
new_assets.implementation: Add a palette entry BIRD.dove and skip the crest for this kind; puff scales the breast ellipse by up to 1.25 and lifts headRot by -0.15. All new fields default off so the regression stays identical.

new_assets.name: palmRiver (with palmTree)
new_assets.description: The single set of the film. palmTree(ctx, x, baseY, {h: 570, lean: 20, fronds: 9}) is a separate reusable piece: a trunk 56 wide at the base tapering to 40, drawn as 12 ringed segments in brown with a slight S lean, a crown heart at the top, nine fronds 230 long (dark green spine with a toothed blade), two coconuts; fronds sway with t. The river half reuses Library river and riverBank where the geometry fits (measure on the set) plus reeds and the snag.
new_assets.implementation: Bake the static parts with bake() per sky preset (day, dawn, dusk); draw fronds, water ripples, reeds and the sun live. Trunk segments with shape() and a dotPat highlight; fronds as a quadratic spine with 10 triangle teeth each side. Reeds: 5 seg() blades per clump with a bend parameter driven by windStreaks. Put palmTree in Library/sets so desert and oasis stories can reuse it.

new_assets.name: chick
new_assets.description: Standalone chick with fields x, y, s, rot, flap, open, gaze, tuft (only the head tuft visible, for the fox mouth).
new_assets.implementation: Lift the single chick drawing out of nestDraw into a small function chick(ctx, P) and call it from nestDraw so the look stays identical.

new_assets.name: fox rear / carry
new_assets.description: Optional fox fields: rear 0..1 (body pivots up about the hind feet to about 60 degrees with both forepaws forward, for paws on a trunk, begging or a pounce start) and carry (a callback drawn at the mouth).
new_assets.implementation: rear: rotate the body group about the hind feet and draw the hind legs unrotated; forepaws use the existing reach geometry. carry: call P.carry(ctx, mouthX, mouthY) after the head. Both default off.

new_assets.name: windStreaks
new_assets.description: Comic wind: 6 to 10 white and pale blue tapering streaks with a curl at the end crossing the panel from a given side (right, left, top or all), strength 0..1; also returns a bend value for reeds, tails and crests.
new_assets.implementation: Seeded K.rng lanes; each streak is a seg() path whose head position is a function of t (loop every 0.9 s); bend = strength * sign of the direction.

new_assets.name: thoughtCloud
new_assets.description: Planned shared effect (already requested by seven stories): a thought cloud large enough to stage action in. Used at 33.1 (her mistaken belief), 61.66 (recap) and 65.4 (the truth).
new_assets.implementation: Wrap the Library cloud() with a clip and a scale transform and call drawInside(ctx) for the small palm, fox and chick.

new_assets.name: fightCloud
new_assets.description: Planned shared effect (KD-005): a churning scuffle cloud with stars and limbs poking out; hides the catch at 146.3.
new_assets.implementation: Eight dustBurst style puffs on seeded orbits, star() pops, two clipped cameo drawings (fox tail, heron leg).

new_assets.name: dayCycle
new_assets.description: Planned shared effect: sky blending day, dusk, night, dawn with sun and moon on arcs; used at 7.68 (waiting on the eggs) and across the dissolve at 79.3.
new_assets.implementation: Cross fade baked sky presets by alpha and move sun()/moon() on a half circle.

owner_questions: The source calls the bird a heron (malik al-hazin) while the English title says Crane: default is to draw a grey heron and label it THE HERON.
The chicks are never shown being eaten: default is that the fox catches each chick in his mouth (only a yellow tuft shows) and trots out of frame.
The heron being caught and eaten is softened: default is a comic dust cloud at the catch, the eating hidden behind shaking reeds with GULP! lettering and drifting feathers.

Additions beyond the script for clarity and humour: the fox really tries to climb and slides down twice at 91.56 to 94.2, and the dove comes down to a driftwood snag to talk to the heron; default is to keep both.
An on-screen counter CHICKS 3, 2, 1 is added, and at the very end the fox passes under the palm while the dove holds firm with her last chick; default is to keep both.
Invented comic lettering: HIGH UP!, ONE CHICK!, SNAP!, COME UP!, THUD!, WIND, POUNCE!, GULP!; default is to keep these eight plus the labels THE HERON and DAYS LATER...
implementation_notes: World is 1400 x 1230 (wider than the template): set WW = 1400 and clamp the camera x to 500/z .. 1400 - 500/z. At z 1.0 only 1000 units of width are visible, so the palm (x 380) and the heron spot (x 1120) share a frame only in FULL (700,615,z1.0) or RIVER_WIDE.

Named camera framings (x, y, zoom): FULL (700,615,1.0); WIDE_PALM (430,590,1.15); NEST_MED (390,360,1.9); NEST_CLOSE (390,300,2.6); FOX_LOW (260,760,1.9); RIVER_WIDE (900,660,1.25); RIVER_TWO from twoShot() about (930,640..720,1.75..1.9).

Key world positions: palm base (380,900); nest seat (385,330); dove on the rim (385,310); fox under the palm x 200 (s 0.8, nose near x 360); bank edge x 780; snag top (860,620); heron fishing spot x 1120, talking spot x 985, feet at y 925 with the front water strip drawn over the lower legs; fox river marks x 640, 700, 760, 820; landing x 1040.

Cue every beat with w(p, n) from timing.json; the times in this plan are word starts on the final MP3. Set LIFE.t = t for automatic blinks and give every character a gaze target on every frame (lookAt, gazePlan).
The three threats must show falling effort (S2 full bluff, S4 half, S7 a yawn) and the three chick states must use the same nest framing so the repeat reads.
The BRAVE pose is a setup and payoff: heron at 72.86, dove copy at 73.88, dove payoff at 87.8, and once more at 158.9. Keep the silhouette identical each time.
The two thought clouds at 33.1 and 65.4 use the same layout (small palm, fox at its foot) with opposite outcomes.
Mask on / mask off for the fox from 97.02: the sweet face only while he is watched; the hungry face when the dove or the heron looks away.
Draw order at the river: back water, far reeds, snag, heron, fox, front water strip, near reeds. Clip the heron and fox legs with the front water strip rather than a second copy.

Sound effects only at the listed times (all in pauses): 4.95, 11.55, 17.6, 23.55, 45.7, 51.75, 59.25, 79.2, 94.25, 127.3, 161.9, with SND master 0.6. The leap at 145.64 has no effect because the narration is continuous there.
Lettering must not cover a face: HIGH UP! beside the trunk, COME UP! on the right of the trunk, POUNCE! above the cloud, GULP! in the reeds, counter at the top left of the picture panel.
All new fields (bird kind dove, puff, fox rear and carry) default off; run node Library/tests/regression.mjs after adding them.
warnings: The heron is a large new character whose tuck pose carries the climax; build and test tuck 0..1 on a still sheet first.

The nest is 570 units above the ground: in any shot wide enough to hold fox and nest the dove is only about 125 px tall, so her acting must be carried by the close shots and by big silhouettes (BRAVE pose, wail).
Library river and riverBank were drawn for the Monkey story with their own bank heights; measure them before reusing, or draw the simple water band described in the set.
nestDraw must draw 2 and 1 chicks cleanly and take per chick acting; check before relying on it.
No pause exists around the leap (145.64) or the second chick drop, so those moments have no sound effect.
The narration is continuous from 138.68 to 161.42; the ending relies on stillness and one drifting feather, so resist adding more lettering there.
